correctness.rationale: The graph Laplacian is symmetric PSD with a simple constant nullspace on connected graphs. For each fixed pair the constant mode cancels; the proper spectral rational representation has numerator degree at most the number of distinct nonzero eigenvalues minus one, bounded by n-2. For paths the positive eigenvalues are simple and each first-edge eigenmode difference is strictly nonzero, permitting arbitrary real residues and hence prescribed simple positive zeros by partial fractions; affine scaling places intrinsic opinions strictly in (0,1). Centered L2 variance is a positive spectral sum whose derivative is strictly negative for nonconstant initial opinions. The exact packaged checker verifies n=3,4,5,6 instances and the n=5 witness; these tests are illustrative, while the cited spectral argument is the general proof. Boundaries t>0, n>=2, f identically zero, simple prescribed roots, and all quantifiers have been checked.

value.rationale: Quantifies maximal complexity of social-influence comparative statics under a natural uniform tie-strength perturbation. Attainability at any prescribed positions on the very sparse connected path proves that repeated pairwise reversals are structural and arbitrarily many with growing network size, even when centered aggregate variance strictly decreases. The result resolves a meaningful distinction between group contraction metrics and individual pair ordering, gives an exact benchmark for sensitivity methods, and does not depend on an isolated unmotivated constant or enumeration. Not claimed to model empirical social polarization.
